approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves a greedy population of molecules using score-weighted breeding, connected-fragment crossover and ordinary atom/bond mutations, with direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange disabled. Each suggestion generates a fresh surplus pool. A Gaussian process learns from the full chronological archive of accepted task-local scores, using folded radius-two chirality-aware Morgan occurrence counts and dot-product count Tanimoto covariance. It normalizes scores with their current mean and population standard deviation, keeps fixed observation noise, and selects new offspring by correlated sampled functions with sequential duplicate masks. Actual accepted scores immediately update the archive and greedy survivors.
approach.novelty: Apply one fixed exponential covariance warp to the existing count similarity: exp(T−1). This retains occurrence information, molecular features and similarity order while adding a common covariance floor and changing conditional regression and sampled-function correlation. Earlier siblings removed multiplicity, unfolded coordinates, added an atom-pair channel, replaced the learner with trees, or projected sampled residuals; this warp changes none of those interfaces. The separate same-round alternatives change the overlap formula or distance geometry. The test asks whether this particular covariance law improves ranking of real evaluated offspring and useful exploration, then meets the complete endpoint criterion.

observed_bottleneck: The completed code Parent n-62daf219c70a has macro mean 0.5956696497334577 and population SD 0.02659287062806747, with seed macros 0.625411930168826, 0.560865654270234 and 0.600731364761313. Only 629 of 4350 accepted offspring strictly beat their best real generating parent; 258 advance the incumbent and 2401 later breed. This is limited productive search with uneven endpoint progress, not proof that a particular covariance is its cause. n-e00db808bbb4 loses 0.051295849138213355 when multiplicity is removed; n-299096e31fe7 loses 0.07686116167690966 when sampled residual influence is removed. n-e75f0f495f9b and n-aa9acd2c2043 show that improved selected-stream prediction, relative parent-win counts or narrower dispersion can coexist with endpoint losses. These controls motivate retaining the count representation and correlated allocator while testing a new covariance operation.
hypothesis: Replace the original dot-product count Tanimoto covariance TDP by the fixed exponential warp K(x,y)=exp(TDP(x,y)-1), lambda=1, on the unchanged folded Morgan integer occurrence vectors, preserving the inherited TDP zero conventions and exact TDP=1 aliases.

finding_summary.headline: Exponential covariance changes allocation but loses 0.03228 despite more local wins
finding_summary.insights: The fixed law clearly executed; missing exposure, broken Gaussian arithmetic, passive fit failure or altered random draws do not explain the endpoint loss. Better prediction on the actively selected stream and more wins against weaker parents did not translate into higher absolute search quality. Productive new typed cores rose only from 280 to 288 and generic cores from 190 to 191; more later breeding also failed to recover the lost endpoints. All 150 terminal offspring in each panel remain censored, and 73 Child versus 50 Parent offspring had later breeding support but were never drawn. The molecular assessment associates the lower results with extended and geometrically uncertain families alongside conventional high-scoring alternatives; fewer unusual local bonds do not establish chemical stability or explain covariance contribution. The experiment narrows the case against this exact lambda-one warp under the tested composition and budget. It cannot tell us whether covariance-floor smoothing, omitted candidate rewards or subsequent feedback caused the loss, and selected-stream diagnostics do not establish pool-wide ranking or calibration. The registered complete gain test ends this exact law; a materially different future law needs a sourced distinguishing experiment.
finding_summary.results: All 15 task/seed evaluations completed. Selected sets changed in 417 of 435 batches, with 1230 active selections outside the passive original set. On the actual Child emissions, MSE fell from 0.007744 with passive original predictions to 0.007064, pair-order accuracy rose from 66.48% to 67.19%, and mean within-batch Spearman rose from 0.4279 to 0.4417. These averages retain the losses: pair ordering worsened on every deco-hop seed and on one sitagliptin seed. Strict best-parent wins increased from 629 to 697 of 4350 offspring, and sequential incumbent advances from 258 to 273, but mean best-generating-parent score fell from 0.47046 to 0.44229; mean offspring score also fell slightly, from 0.38526 to 0.38235. Total incumbent gain fell from 5.80766 to 5.32350. Final macro score decreased from 0.59566965 to 0.56339196, a mean loss of 0.03227769 against the required gain of 0.002. Paired seed changes were −0.06839278, +0.00744768, −0.03588798; Child population SD was 0.00472367 versus 0.02659287. Median-2 improved in every seed, while deco-hop and docking lost in every seed. There were six task/seed wins and nine losses.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families and cyclic amines emerge, with reactive local bonds, uncertain polycycle geometry and unassigned stereo
molecular.overall_character: All 15 Child and all 15 published code-Parent trajectory paths and corresponding logs were present and read through the immutable request/evidence-index scope. No task is missing: each task has 900 accepted trajectory records, including 870 optimizer proposals; each cell has 300 records. Child_complete=true and paired_complete=true with matched Search seeds 0/1/2, Parent n-62daf219c70a; this is a complete paired comparison, not merely a complete Child. Fake smoke is outside these trusted inputs. Accepted-record labels join all observations without mismatch. The Child chemistry spans aromatic carboxamides, extended azaaryl assemblies, ring/flexible amines, nitrogen-carbonyl polycycles and fluorinated imino/dione systems. Rings and aromaticity are rich, consistent with optimizer ring-text incidences 0.9954 to 1.0 and aromatic-text incidences 0.9862 to 1.0. These counters indicate occurrence in SMILES, not atom fraction. Formal-charge and stereo text incidences are zero; neutral SMILES still contain basic amines. RDKit 2023.09.6 descriptors over complete accepted optimizer streams find 2184/4350 Child versus 2408/4350 Parent molecules with potential unspecified tetrahedral centres and zero specified-centre molecules in either. Heteroatom-halogen bonds occur in 828/4350 versus 1329/4350 and O-O bonds in 66/4350 versus 273/4350; lower incidence does not establish a chemical intervention or measured safety. Many framework types are explored, but seed-local leaders repeatedly refine limited families. Overall diversity is moderate; synthetic plausibility questionable and drug-likeness weak because familiar functionality is repeatedly combined with reactive bond environments, high mass in extended families and geometrically uncertain rings. No atom inheritance, synthesis, stability, protonation, conformation or biological activity was measured. The digest final excerpt only contains late seed-2 proposals, so complete trajectory maxima were used for seed endpoints. Recorded paired seed macro deltas are 0: -0.0683927816206981, 1: +0.00744768230021597, 2: -0.035887981327994; paired mean delta -0.032277693549492024. These are inherited evaluation facts, not a molecular-role decision about success or activation. Across accepted Child versus Parent offspring, strict best-parent beats are 697 versus 629 and sequential incumbent advances 273 versus 258. Novel typed cores conditional on either positive event number 288 versus 280, of which 284 versus 274 are used in later actual breed requests and 157 versus 151 have an accepted direct descendant scoring above that source. Generic equivalents are 191 versus 190, later breeders 188 versus 186, and sources with a higher-scoring direct descendant 102 versus 107. For these novelty/event cohorts, typed nonterminal records without later breeding are 1 versus 3 with terminal censored records 3 versus 3; generic counts are 1 versus 2 and terminal 2 versus 2. All accepted offspring retain nonterminal no-later-breeding counts 1546 versus 1799 and terminal records 150 versus 150. Observed nonuse is not proof of absent survivor support; support probabilities were not measured in this molecular audit. Positive source/descendant cohorts overlap and are not additive independent contributions. The generic descendant counterexample and every signed task/seed endpoint are retained. New typed/generic cores are exact graph descriptors relative to earlier accepted molecules; empty cores are one explicit acyclic class. All 8500 unique SMILES across Child/Parent parse; typed/generic descriptors have no errors. Core matches do not establish shared ancestry or chemical mediation. Read-only audit definitions, all 30 cells, per-event novelty/use joins and hashes are in /projects/standard/adeshwal/shared/zhou2577/SPIRAL/.slots/round-0026-slot-2/molecular_audit.json. No pool-wide novelty, unselected/passive molecule labels, atom provenance, positive-but-unused support, or causal covariance contribution is inferred.

per_task.generated_character: Compact substituted fused aromatic amides dominate. Seed 0 develops methoxy/methyl/fluoromethyl indole anilides, including an N-fluoro amide and N-amino ring nitrogen. Seed 1 forms an additional oxygen/nitrogen ring with a pyridyl thiourea-like carbonyl replacement. Seed 2 keeps a methylated methoxyindole carboxamide linked to a cyanophenyl ring; its ordinary N-H indole analogue is also near the highest recorded score. The best molecules have 25 heavy atoms in each seed; RDKit ring/aromatic-ring counts are respectively 3/3, 4/2 and 3/3. Recognizable indole/anilide/nitrile chemistry coexists with chemically unusual N-S, N-F and ring N-O arrangements. Digest optimizer-only string incidences: ring closure 0.9954, aromatic text 0.9954; mean SMILES length 44.3. These are molecule-text incidences and length, not atom fractions or perceived ring counts. Optimizer typed/generic Murcko unique-core counts, retaining the empty acyclic class, Child versus Parent in seed order: 0: 74/35 versus 129/61; 1: 135/70 versus 85/39; 2: 61/31 versus 117/57.
liabilities: The seed-0 leading example has N-F on the amide and an N-N attachment at ring nitrogen; seed-2 leaders include N-S and adjacent ring nitrogen/oxygen. These demand separate stability and synthetic scrutiny from ordinary aryl C-F substitution.
Peripheral high-score ties include sulfur modifications and unusual valence forms. Parseability and score do not establish stability or an accessible synthesis.
missing_features: The output does not consistently retain conventional N-H or stable carbon-substitution environments around a favorable compact aromatic/carboxamide arrangement. The nearly tied ordinary N-H analogue is a counterexample to any claim that the unusual N-S group is required.
Broader independent compact frameworks preserving the combined functional arrangement are not demonstrated by the recurrent leading family; many variants alter substituents or close related rings.
No target-specific missing pharmacophore can be inferred from these scalar scores; donors, heteroaromatic nitrogens and nitriles are present in the output.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original chemical gap source n-c55c3d520a2c, reproduced in accepted same-code baseline n-62daf219c70a and re-observed in n-07dd356cb779 on Search seeds 0/1/2, 300 accepted observations per task under the frozen Research in Depth profile. This is chemistry association, not component attribution. Child accepted outputs contain 828/4350 optimizer molecules with N/O/S-halogen bonds and 66/4350 with O-O bonds; Parent has 1329/4350 and 273/4350. High recorded-score examples still include N-F, N-S, O-Cl, O-F, S-Cl and chloromethyl ethers. An ordinary N-H aromatic carboxamide nearly ties its unusual N-S analogue, and successful conventional cyclic-amine families exist. The capability is present intermittently rather than absent; lower incidence is not demonstrated stability.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve conventional local bond environments around otherwise useful aromatic and heterocyclic frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator could preserve learned favorable functional arrangements while proposing conventional local bond-environment alternatives. Any modification needs a separately registered contribution experiment; do not hardcode an objective, copy a high-scoring reactive substituent, or discard counterexamples.

This is chemistry association, not component attribution. Leaders include fluorinated four-membered unsaturated rings, exocyclic unsaturation attached to small fused rings, crowded N/O bridges and expanded heterocycles. Large extended aromatic assemblies coexist with a compact higher-scoring Parent arrangement, so adding atoms or rings is not a general remedy. Murcko and parse success establish graph descriptors only.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently distinguish representable cyclic graphs from credible geometry and accessible synthetic topology.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring transformations could account for ring size, junction geometry, unsaturation and bridge connectivity while retaining diverse alternatives suggested by actual feedback. Preserve legitimate small rings and conventional cyclic amines as counterexamples; geometry-aware proposals require evaluation rather than assuming that a global ring-count restriction fixes this gap.

Complete descriptors find 2184/4350 Child and 2408/4350 Parent optimizer molecules with potential unassigned tetrahedral centres, with zero specified-centre molecules in either panel. Dense fused-ring, substituted cyclic-amine and sulfoxide-containing families illustrate the issue; aromatic leaders without potential centres are retained as counterexamples. Descriptor conventions do not measure configurational stability or all possible axial/double-bond stereo.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not specify stereochemical identity when it generates potentially stereogenic saturated or bridged centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representation and graph transformations could preserve or resolve stereochemistry where chemically relevant, distinguishing achiral and configurationally labile centres. This is a structural identity gap; the records do not establish that stereochemical expansion improves scalar scores.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
